local_evidence: Blacktown City Council stated in August 2024 that requests for year-round cricket competitions could not be met because of a shortage of fields. Blacktown City & District Cricket Association then won Cricket NSW's 2025/26 Junior Initiative award for its Under-9s Transition Competition.
evidence_signal: Strong participation ecosystem plus explicit field shortage
next_question: Which western/north-west Blacktown catchments have the largest mismatch between junior growth and playable cricket-field capacity?

local_evidence: Ipswich forecasts very rapid future population growth. In 2026 Council sought cricket/AFL users for a new South Ripley sports oval. evidence_signal: Demand and delivery both growing; new capacity coming online
phase14_interpretation: Activate/accelerate candidate with ongoing capacity build

evidence_signal: Strong demographic case and improving cricket infrastructure; direct participation evidence limited

local_evidence: Maitland City Council began construction in 2025 on Chisholm's first $10m sportsground, including a turf cricket wicket, specifically citing the area's growing population. Cricket NSW also highlighted a six-week all-girls cricket clinic in Maitland for ages 7–14 in 2025, and its competition framework includes Maitland district senior and junior associations.
evidence_signal: Regional growth plus visible infrastructure and girls' participation initiatives
phase14_interpretation: Strong regional comparator / targeted growth case
